name: Joy Division
label: Factory Records
lede: Four lads from Salford and Macclesfield saw the Sex Pistols, bought instruments, and in under three years made two albums that Factory Records was built on. Then their singer died the night before their first American tour, and the other three kept going under a new name.

eras.title: The Pistols come to Manchester
eras.text: The Sex Pistols played Manchester in June 1976, and people in the room went home and formed bands. Two of them were Salford schoolfriends who couldn't play yet. Within a year they had a singer from Macclesfield, a name borrowed from a Bowie song, and a drummer problem.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joy Division · Wikipedia: Peter Hook
years.h: Sumner and Hook watch the Sex Pistols, and Hook borrows £35 for a bass
years.p: [[Bernard Sumner|6fa2e161-200e-475a-8492-3755594581f9]] and [[Peter Hook|73e7c483-9f3e-4a72-a359-582452fbaeac]] are at the Pistols' gig at the Lesser Free Trade Hall. Hook's mother lends him the money for his first bass.
years.xp: Sumner said later that the Pistols "destroyed the myth of being a pop star, of a musician being some kind of god that you had to worship." If those four could do it, so could two lads from Salford.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joy Division · Wikipedia: Ian Curtis
years.h: Ian Curtis answers an ad at the Virgin shop
years.p: [[Ian Curtis|10ae1bf6-88b2-4fb4-8fbe-8227a49803d3]], a civil servant from Macclesfield, answers a notice in Manchester's Virgin Records shop and gets the job without an audition.
years.xp:
Sumner's test was simple: Curtis was all right to get on with, "and that's what we based the whole group on. If we liked someone, they were in."

Curtis had married Deborah Woodruff in August 1975. By day he worked for the civil service, later as an assistant disablement resettlement officer at the Macclesfield employment exchange.

years.cap: Fans queuing to see Warsaw, Manchester, 1977
years.h: Warsaw's first gig, under Buzzcocks at the Electric Circus
years.p: The band had been the Stiff Kittens for a while, a name from [[Buzzcocks|31e9c35b-2675-4632-8596-f9bd9286f6c8]]' Richard Boon and Pete Shelley. They go on as Warsaw, after Bowie's 'Warszawa', supporting Buzzcocks, Penetration and [[John Cooper Clarke|7df6e6eb-8e3a-4402-a243-b5b01f0d9bec]].
years.xp: Tony Tabac played drums. Paul Morley reviewed it for NME and Ian Wood for Sounds, so a band on its first night got national print.

years.h: Drummer Steve Brotherdale is sent to check a tyre, and the van leaves
years.p: Steve Brotherdale replaces Tony Tabac in June. After a demo session the others ask him to check a flat tyre, then drive off without him.

years.h: Stephen Morris answers an ad and keeps the drum stool for good
years.p: [[Stephen Morris|b3036249-8b39-4d02-a312-d31a63497bbc]], from Macclesfield like Curtis, makes it a quartet. Deborah Curtis wrote that he "fitted perfectly."

years.h: Warsaw cuts its first EP at Pennine Sound, Oldham
years.p: Four songs that become An Ideal for Living. Warsaw plays its last show under that name on New Year's Eve at the Swinging Apple, Liverpool.

eras.title: A name from a novel, a fight with a TV host
eras.text: Warsaw clashed with a London band called Warsaw Pakt, so they took a darker name. That year they found the three men who would shape everything after: a manager, a TV presenter with a record label in his head, and a producer who heard space where the band heard noise.

years.h: First gig as Joy Division, at Pip's Disco in Manchester
years.p: The new name came from the brothel wing in the 1955 novella House of Dolls. It drew accusations of Nazi chic that followed the band, and the next one, for years.

years.cap: Tony Wilson at the Russell Club on a Factory night
years.h: Curtis has a go at Tony Wilson at Rafters, and it works
years.p: At the Stiff/Chiswick Challenge at Rafters, Curtis tells Granada's [[Tony Wilson|124a6f5d-b2e0-4a75-95ad-db4c38063e02]] off for never putting the band on TV. Wilson promises to, and [[Rob Gretton|41b55fab-da3b-4ecf-a67d-aeeec338a9c5]] signs on as manager.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Gretton's "dogged determination" for much of what followed. He ran the band's business, paid attention to everything and later became a partner in Factory.

years.h: The band presses An Ideal for Living itself
years.p: A self-released EP from the Pennine Sound session, with a Sumner drawing of a Hitler Youth drummer on the sleeve.

years.h: Wilson keeps his word: 'Shadowplay' on So It Goes
years.p: Wilson introduces the band on his Granada music show. It's Joy Division's first TV appearance.

years.src: Wikipedia: Joy Division · Wikipedia: Factory Records
years.h: FAC 2: Joy Division open Factory's first record
years.p: Two Joy Division tracks share a double 7-inch with [[The Durutti Column|aaddb5e3-f8a5-4a9d-8674-f885112ecf0e]], [[John Dowie|e7c6f981-c0eb-444d-a6e1-98b430e77ea2]] and [[Cabaret Voltaire|439a29ad-f4ef-4857-a7cd-3d4a551056c8]]. To join Factory, the band bought its way out of a deal with RCA.
years.xp: Paul Morley in NME called them "the missing link" between Elvis Presley and [[Siouxsie and the Banshees|78ea5ea1-3c4d-4b7e-ac5d-68900319ebe2]].

years.src: Wikipedia: Joy Division · Wikipedia: Ian Curtis
years.h: Curtis has his first major seizure on the drive home from London
years.p: After a gig at the Hope and Anchor, Curtis has a seizure in the car and is taken to hospital. He is diagnosed with epilepsy the next month.

eras.title: Hannett's room, Saville's pulsar
eras.text: Martin Hannett took four fast, loud men into Strawberry Studios and gave them back a record full of space, echo and studio lift. They hated it at first. Factory pressed 10,000 anyway, and the record made the label.

years.cap: Joy Division in Hulme, Manchester, January 1979
years.src: Wikipedia: Joy Division · Wikipedia: Ian Curtis
years.h: Curtis makes the NME cover, and the band records for John Peel
years.p: Curtis is on the January 13 cover of NME. That month the band records its first session for [[John Peel|e4dec348-ad10-43b6-a2b1-c22aab890675]] at BBC Radio 1. Doctors confirm his epilepsy on January 23.

q: I was convinced that it was just sexier in black.
years.src: Wikipedia: Unknown Pleasures · Wikipedia: Joy Division
years.h: Unknown Pleasures, FACT 10, out of three weekends in Stockport
years.p: Hannett records Curtis's vocal on 'Insight' down a telephone line and works in a smashed bottle, someone eating crisps and the studio lift. Half of the first 10,000 sell in two weeks.
years.xp:
Sumner felt Hannett had "inflicted this dark, doomy mood" and toned down the guitars. Hook thought it "sounded like Pink Floyd." Morris and Curtis were happy, and Hook later conceded Hannett "created the Joy Division sound."

Jon Savage in Melody Maker called it an "opaque manifesto." Wilson credited the album with turning Factory into a force outside the major-label system.

years.h: Saville turns a dead star into a sleeve
years.p: [[Peter Saville|e61408b0-767c-4dde-ad88-a052456efcfe]] takes a plot of pulses from the first pulsar ever found, printed in The Cambridge Encyclopaedia of Astronomy, and flips it white on black. No band name, no title on the front.
years.xp: The image had been drawn up by radio astronomer Harold Craft for his 1970 dissertation. The band wanted it black on white; Saville reversed it.

years.h: The band's only nationwide TV spot, on BBC2's Something Else
years.p: It follows a Granada TV spot on July 20.

years.cap: Joy Division at the Apollo, Manchester, October 27, 1979, on the Buzzcocks tour
years.h: Twenty-four dates opening for Buzzcocks, and the day jobs go
years.p: The UK tour pays enough that the four quit their regular jobs. The non-album single 'Transmission' follows near the end of the year.

eras.title: The flight was booked for May 19
eras.text: Joy Division were bigger than ever and Curtis was getting worse. The band made Closer in a fortnight in Islington, filmed one video themselves, and booked a flight to America. Curtis died the night before it.

years.cap: Joy Division live at Plan K, Brussels
years.h: A European tour, and two grand mal seizures
years.p: Joy Division tour the Continent. Curtis has two grand mal seizures in the last two months of the run.

years.h: Thirteen days at Britannia Row make Closer
years.p: Hannett produces from March 18 to 30 in Islington, London. Hook felt the effects buried his bass; Pitchfork later called the result sepulchral.

years.h: Bottles fly at Derby Hall, Bury, when Curtis can't perform
years.p: Curtis is too ill to play the whole set. Singers from [[Crispy Ambulance|3420e6bc-8551-4c6c-86ca-c13a3115edd3]] and [[A Certain Ratio|73577e86-4da8-4d76-949d-34c757e053be]] stand in, and the crowd starts throwing bottles.
years.xp: The night before, Curtis had taken an overdose of phenobarbitone, his anti-seizure medication. Several April gigs were cancelled afterwards.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Will Tear Us Apart
years.h: The 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' video, shot in their rehearsal room
years.p: Filmed at T.J. Davidson's studio in Knott Mill, Manchester. It's the only promo video Joy Division ever made.

years.cap: Joy Division on stage at High Hall, University of Birmingham, May 2, 1980
years.h: The last gig, Birmingham University, and the only 'Ceremony'
years.p: At the High Hall they play 'Ceremony', one of the last songs Curtis wrote, for the first and only time. The recording ends up on Still.

years.src: Wikipedia: Ian Curtis · Wikipedia: Joy Division
years.h: Ian Curtis dies at home in Macclesfield, aged 23
years.p: Curtis hanged himself in the kitchen at 77 Barton Street. Joy Division were due to fly out of Manchester for their first North American tour the next day.
years.xp:
He had spent the evening watching Werner Herzog's Stroszek and listening to Iggy Pop's The Idiot. Deborah Curtis found him. He was cremated on May 23.

"I think all of us made the mistake of not thinking his suicide was going to happen," Wilson said. Morris said it was only after Curtis died that the band sat down and properly listened to the lyrics.

eras.title: Number 13, then number 6
eras.text: The records Curtis left behind did what the band never had while he was alive: they charted. The other three agreed early that the Joy Division name would end with him.

years.src: Wikipedia: Love Will Tear Us Apart
years.h: 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' reaches No. 13
years.p: Cut twice, at Pennine Sound in January and Strawberry in March, the single tops the UK indie chart. Morris says he still grits his teeth at Hannett calling him back at 4 a.m. to redo the snare.

years.big: "We've got a tomb on the cover"
years.h: Closer comes out with a tomb on the sleeve
years.p: Saville and Martyn Atkins had chosen Bernard Pierre Wolff's photo of the Appiani family tomb in Genoa's Staglieno cemetery before Curtis died. The album reaches No. 6 and is NME's album of the year.
years.xp: Saville's line came when he heard the news. Charles Shaar Murray wrote in NME that Closer was "as magnificent a memorial ... as any post-Presley popular musician could have."

years.h: Sumner, Hook and Morris play their first gig as a trio
years.p: Unnamed, they play Manchester's Beach Club. By the autumn, with [[Gillian Gilbert|c970c5cd-facf-4c49-babf-a5b688c1ec40]] on keyboards, they are [[New Order|f1106b17-dcbb-45f6-b938-199ccfab50cc]].

years.h: Still gathers the leftovers and the final night
years.p: A double album of studio rarities plus the whole Birmingham University show from May 2, 1980.

eras.title: The pulsar on a million T-shirts
eras.text: Joy Division lasted under three years as Joy Division. Everything after, the compilations, the films, the reissues and the arguments between former bandmates, kept the four of them in the same sentence.

years.h: Substance puts the singles back in print
years.p: Factory collects the out-of-print singles, 'Transmission' and 'Atmosphere' among them. After Factory's 1992 collapse, London Records takes over the catalogue.

years.h: 24 Hour Party People puts Factory on screen
years.p: Michael Winterbottom's film casts Sean Harris as Curtis, John Simm as Sumner and Ralf Little as Hook, with Steve Coogan as Wilson.
years.xp: Wilson on its accuracy: "It's all true, it's all not true. It's not a fucking documentary."

years.cap: Sam Riley as Ian Curtis in Control, 2007
years.h: Anton Corbijn opens Cannes' Directors' Fortnight with Control
years.p: Photographer [[Anton Corbijn|86422a7c-ab5c-4343-8710-a8c1e871abd3]] films Deborah Curtis's memoir Touching from a Distance with Sam Riley as Curtis. Grant Gee's documentary Joy Division follows the same year.

years.cap: Ian Curtis's original memorial stone, Macclesfield Cemetery, 2008
years.src: Wikipedia: Love Will Tear Us Apart
years.h: Curtis's memorial stone is stolen, and replaced
years.p: The stone at Macclesfield Cemetery, inscribed with the title 'Love Will Tear Us Apart' at Deborah Curtis's choice, is taken and replaced in 2008.

years.cap: Peter Hook and the Light on stage
years.h: Hook starts playing the albums in full with the Light
years.p: Peter Hook and the Light begin with Unknown Pleasures start to finish, and go on to the rest of the Joy Division and New Order catalogue.

years.h: Unknown Pleasures reaches No. 5, forty years late
years.p: The album had first charted at No. 71 on a 1980 reissue.

years.src: Rock and Roll Hall of Fame
years.h: Into the Rock and Roll Hall of Fame, with New Order, as one act
years.p: The Hall inducts Curtis, Sumner, Hook, Morris and Gilbert together as Joy Division/New Order.

sources.title: Wikipedia: Love Will Tear Us Apart
